The Mets plan to stick with Devin Williams as their closer in 2027, per Pat Ragazzo.

Williams had a rough first season in New York, posting a 4.43 ERA and 1.57 WHIP over 40.2 innings.

There were some positives, though. He struck out nearly 29% of hitters and converted 16 of 19 save chances.

Kodai Senga also pitched well out of the bullpen, but Williams looks like he'll get the first shot at closing again. The Mets will likely want a backup plan if he struggles.

Claude Code on desktop can now test your app on an iPhone Duo in the iOS simulator.

> Your app runs on the Duo next to your conversation, and Claude can fold the device closed, half open, or open to check each layout. It can also set a half-open hinge angle from 1 to 179 degrees, and you can fold the device yourself with the pose buttons in the pane.

> To try it, name the iPhone Duo in your request, like asking Claude to check a settings screen closed, half open, and open. If you work in a terminal instead, the Xcode plugin is now in the official Claude Code plugin marketplace. With it, Claude can build, run, and test your app and render SwiftUI previews.

> It's a public beta on macOS that needs Claude Desktop v4.29.0 or later and Xcode 27.1 or later with the iOS 27.1 simulator runtime. The simulator pane is on Pro, Max, Ultra, Team, and Enterprise plans, except in Enterprise organizations with a HIPAA configuration, and it isn't available through a third-party provider. Screenshots Claude takes of the device are sent to Anthropic, so the docs advise against signing in to real accounts on it.

note_tweet.text:
Obsidian official Agent Skills, 52.9K stars: seven skills that teach an agent to operate your vault
The repo is not new. Obsidian opened it on January 2, 2026 with Markdown and Bases, and Canvas followed days later. The CLI and Defuddle arrived in February, Knap in September, and on November 11 the older ob-cli skill was rebuilt as obsidian-headless. On November 14, CEO kepano posted that there are now seven skills "that teach your agents how to fully operate your vaults and wikis." That post had 90,302 views and 2,624 bookmarks. The plugin is at version 1.2.0, MIT licensed.
What each one actually does:
- obsidian-markdown: writes Obsidian-flavored notes with wikilinks, embeds, callouts and properties, not generic Markdown
- obsidian-bases: creates .base database files with views, filters, formulas, summaries and kanban
- json-canvas: creates .canvas boards with nodes, edges and groups
- obsidian-cli: drives a running Obsidian app from the terminal, including search, create, rename so links update, and plugin or theme debugging
- obsidian-headless: syncs or publishes from the command line without the desktop app (open beta)
- defuddle: strips a web page down to clean Markdown to save tokens
- knap: renders Markdown templates from JSON or CSV, including batch file generation
Minimal install, inside a Claude Code session:
/plugin marketplace add obsidianmd/obsidian-skills
/plugin install obsidian@obsidian-skills
From a terminal, use the same two lines starting with "claude plugin". To get skills added later: claude plugin update obsidian@obsidian-skills
Codex: codex plugin marketplace add obsidianmd/obsidian-skills, then install Obsidian from the plugin directory. Cursor: install Obsidian from the Cursor Marketplace. OpenCode: clone the full repo into ~/.opencode/skills/obsidian-skills, not just the inner skills folder. Manual Claude Code path: copy plugins/obsidian/skills/ to .claude/skills/ at the vault root.
How to check it worked
Ask the agent for one short note with a wikilink, a property and a callout, then open it in reading view. For the CLI, the app must be running; try obsidian help. Defuddle and Knap aren't bundled, and the skills are supposed to ask before installing them from npm.
Limits and risks
Markdown, Bases and Canvas are format guides, and kepano says you don't need the app open to use them. The CLI needs the Obsidian 1.12.7+ installer, Settings → General → Command line interface turned on, and a running app. Don't install the unrelated npm package called obsidian-cli. Headless needs Node.js 22+, and real Sync or Publish needs those paid subscriptions. The official docs say back up first and don't run desktop Sync and Headless Sync on the same device. Knap needs Node.js 20+ and won't overwrite files unless you pass --overwrite. Defuddle's README still calls it a work in progress.
These skills can write, rename, move and trash notes, and the plugin warns that vault content you ask about can be sent to the AI model. Start on a copy of your vault. Some replies said models already handle Obsidian fine without them, and kepano agreed the latest models have gotten very good.
Best first use
Copy a small vault, install the plugin, and have it turn one public article into a dated note with tags and a wikilink back to an existing topic. Then open it and check that the links, properties and callouts actually render.
https://t.co/yInG4DcFS1
